fixes.old: A 529 plan serves families focused strictly on tax-free college savings, while a custodial brokerage account under the Uniform Transfers to Minors Act (UTMA) or Uniform Gifts to Minors Act (UGMA) fits parents who want flexible spending without contribution caps. A custodial Roth IRA works for a teenager with earned income, a Coverdell Education Savings Account (ESA) covers smaller education goals up to $2,000 annually, and high-yield savings accounts or Treasury inflation-protected I bonds protect cash needed on a shorter timeline. If you weigh a [Trump Account vs a 529](/compare/trump-account-vs-529/), the broader utility of these established vehicles often outweighs the restrictions tied to the newer model.
fixes.new: A 529 plan fits families saving for college, and its qualified education withdrawals are tax-free. A custodial brokerage account under the Uniform Transfers to Minors Act (UTMA) or Uniform Gifts to Minors Act (UGMA) fits parents who want flexible spending with no contribution cap. A custodial Roth IRA fits a teenager with earned income. A Coverdell Education Savings Account (ESA) covers smaller education goals, up to $2,000 a year per child. A high-yield savings account or I bonds hold money needed sooner or kept safe. To compare the first option with the Trump Account directly, read [Trump Account vs a 529](/compare/trump-account-vs-529/).
fixes.why: Overloaded sentences (45+ words, 5 goals chained); 'Treasury inflation-protected I bonds' is not on the closed fact list and reads as TIPS (I bonds are not); closing sentence ('broader utility ... often outweighs the restrictions tied to the newer model') is a vague hedged judgment with a coy 'newer model'.

fixes.old: Our guide on [how a Trump Account works](/guides/trump-accounts/) breaks down how these outside contributions share an annual $5,000 cap with family deposits for 2026 and 2027.
fixes.new: Employer and family contributions share an annual $5,000 cap for 2026 and 2027, while qualified general contributions fall outside that cap. [How a Trump Account works](/guides/trump-accounts/) covers the full contribution rules.
fixes.why: Wrong: per Notice 2025-68 only employer and other-source contributions share the $5,000 cap; qualified general contributions, the pilot deposit and rollovers are exempt. Contradicts the closed fact list.
